correctness.rationale: Exact conditional transition expectations under 2(n−1) total degree yield the root degree-one survival law, equal degree-two mass, the two conditional leaf regressions, and the mixed covariance difference equation. Nonnegative increments prove the precise sign classification. Central-binomial asymptotics and explicit root-degree and leaf-count variance recurrences prove the covariance/correlation rates. The independent full-attachment-history enumerator passed 397 tests through n=9 and recurrence/asymptotic corroboration. Exceptional n=2,3 cases are separately specified. Finite experiments do not prove infinite claims.

originality.rationale: The claim is not the known marginal leaf distribution, nor a fixed old-vertex degree law or a covariance of two global degree classes. It combines a strict fall in the conditional expected total leaves between root degrees 1 and 2, a simultaneously positive all-size root/global covariance, and its square-root asymptotic. Primary literature and scientific record searches did not identify direct implication. Earlier implicit derivations remain a documented priority risk.

value.rationale: Global leaf count quantifies preferential-attachment tree shape while the initial-vertex degree captures the age-specific hub. The two lowest root degrees have equal mass, so their strict reverse regression is a natural effect, and the simultaneous positive aggregate covariance proves that nonmonotone conditional dependence survives all finite n≥4. The exact coefficient and √n covariance growth quantify a structural coupling distinct from uniform recursive-tree behavior.
